outcome.technical:
(1)+(2) tools/sweep-selftests.py: the legacy-locale decision is now the pure locale_decision(os_name, reported, encoding, locale_vars) over the (preferred, filesystem) pair a child reports under the pins; legacy_locale_verdict (replacing legacy_locale_problem) runs the one-time probe LOCALE_PROBE, which now prints locale.getpreferredencoding(False) AND sys.getfilesystemencoding(). Pins are kept only for a non-UTF-8 preferred + UTF-8 filesystem pair (macOS); a non-UTF-8 filesystem encoding (linux C locale) pins no locale and runs the stdio half alone; a UTF-8 preferred encoding refuses as could-not-run; windows is not asked and not refused. main prints the verdict's line (which half ran and why) before the budget line and threads verdict['locale'] through sweep(locale_vars=) -> run_one(locale_vars=) -> locale_pins. New case (the tests.add title) feeds the macOS, linux and windows pairs plus a UTF-8 pair and checks pins, refusal and printed line in both directions; the existing could-not-run case now asserts windows' contract (no check, no refusal) instead of failing there, and the bare-read case asserts failure only where this machine's verdict pins. CONTRIBUTING.md's encoding-pass paragraph and the file's usage line updated. (3) sn6 layer, traced: audit-lookup.py's __main__ runs main through _output.terse_cli, which holds stdout in a StringIO; write_exact sees no .buffer on the StringIO and writes text into it; terse_cli then re-emits the held text with sys.stdout.write through the TEXT layer, which on Windows writes every LF as CRLF, so the diff's embedded CRLF leaves as CR CR LF; drive-phase run_verb's _verb_text then reads CR CR LF as two line breaks. Reproduced on macOS with a sitecustomize that reconfigures child stdout to newline='
' (buffer untouched): HEAD in-process gives '-v0

-kept

' exactly as the Windows CI log showed. Fix: audit-lookup.py passes long_form=('--read',) so --read runs unheld and write_exact reaches the buffer; drive-phase.py run_verb gains record=True (stdout decoded, no newline translation, _record_text) used only by run_brief, with the docstring naming message verbs vs the one record verb; drive-phase's __main__ runs `brief` outside terse_cli with out=write_record (UTF-8 bytes to stdout.buffer). New stage bc-block in test_drive_phase.py drives a task over a CRLF source to the reviewer dispatch and compares the written brief's bytes with brief <id> in process and through the command line, both under the Windows-shaped stdout emulation. Runs: test_drive_phase --selftest --stage bc-block 1/1 after the fix, 0/1 on a HEAD archive with only the test file copied; sweep-selftests --selftest 98/98; plain sweep `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet` exit 0, 335/335 files ok; `--quiet --encoding cp1252` exit 0, 335/335 ok, printing 'encoding pass: both halves ran ... preferred encoding US-ASCII and filesystem encoding utf-8'. Also ran (beyond own-tests, at the orchestrator's prompt or as a check): ruff check plugins/audit tools exit 0, vermin exit 0, tools/gate-parity.py exit 0. One edit to test_drive_phase.py (registering the stage and removing an unused variable) was made with a python one-liner instead of the Edit tool, against the orchestrator's rule; content is in the diff. Linux behaviour is not run here: it is asserted through the pure decision fed linux's reported pair.
